points.place: 安大略省格雷文赫斯特
points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 白求恩出生于安大略省格雷文赫斯特的一个牧师家庭。他的父亲是苏格兰裔加拿大人，母亲是英格兰裔。白求恩自幼展现出对医学的兴趣，但最初学习神学。1907年进入多伦多大学医学院，1912年毕业。这段时期奠定了他的医学基础，并培养了他对社会不公的敏感意识。
points.descriptionEn: Bethune was born in Gravenhurst, Ontario, to a Presbyterian minister of Scottish descent and an English mother. He showed early interest in medicine but initially studied theology. He entered the University of Toronto Medical School in 1907 and graduated in 1912. This period established his medical foundation and developed his sensitivity to social injustice.

points.title: 行医探索
points.description: 毕业后，白求恩在底特律和纽约等地行医。他曾在底特律的亨利·福特医院工作，后来在蒙特利尔开设私人诊所。这一时期，他开始关注肺结核的治疗，并发明了多种医疗设备，包括移动输血车。他的医疗创新和对患者关怀的态度赢得了声誉，但也因激进的政治观点而引起争议。
points.descriptionEn: After graduation, Bethune practiced medicine in Detroit and New York. He worked at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit and later opened a private practice in Montreal. During this time, he focused on tuberculosis treatment and invented several medical devices, including a mobile blood transfusion unit. His medical innovations and compassionate care earned him respect, but his radical political views also sparked controversy.

points.title: 医疗改革
points.description: 在蒙特利尔期间，白求恩成为胸外科专家，并致力于医疗改革。他建立了蒙特利尔肺结核防治中心，推行免费医疗理念。他积极参与社会活动，支持西班牙内战中的共和派，组织医疗队前往西班牙。这段经历使他更加坚定了医疗应该为穷人服务的信念，并开始思考如何将医学与社会变革相结合。
points.descriptionEn: In Montreal, Bethune became a thoracic surgery specialist and dedicated himself to medical reform. He established the Montreal TB clinic and promoted the concept of free healthcare. He actively participated in social activities, supporting the Republicans in the Spanish Civil War and organizing medical teams to Spain. This experience strengthened his belief that medicine should serve the poor and began his thinking on combining medicine with social change.

points.title: 西班牙战场
points.description: 白求恩前往西班牙内战前线，为共和派军队提供医疗援助。他发明了移动输血车，大大提高了前线伤员的存活率。在西班牙，他建立了第一个战地血库，培训医护人员，并撰写了关于战地医疗的著作。这段经历让他深刻认识到战争对平民的伤害，也锻炼了他在极端条件下的医疗组织能力，为他后来在中国的工作奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Bethune went to the front lines of the Spanish Civil War to provide medical aid to Republican forces. He invented the mobile blood transfusion unit, significantly improving survival rates for wounded soldiers. In Spain, he established the first mobile blood bank, trained medical personnel, and wrote about battlefield medicine. This experience made him deeply aware of war's impact on civilians and honed his ability to organize medical care under extreme conditions, laying the foundation for his later work in China.

points.title: 中国岁月
points.description: 1938年，白求恩受加拿大共产党和美国共产党派遣，来到中国延安，为八路军提供医疗援助。他创建了八路军战地医院，培训医护人员，改进医疗设备。在艰苦的条件下，他坚持为伤员服务，经常连续工作数十小时。1939年11月，在一次手术中因感染败血症不幸逝世，年仅49岁。毛泽东为他撰写了著名的《纪念白求恩》一文，高度评价他的国际主义精神，使他成为中国家喻户晓的国际友人。
points.descriptionEn: In 1938, Bethune was sent to Yan'an, China, by the Canadian Communist Party and the American Communist Party to provide medical aid to the Eighth Route Army. He established field hospitals, trained medical personnel, and improved medical equipment. Under harsh conditions, he insisted on treating wounded soldiers, often working continuously for dozens of hours. In November 1939, he died of septicemia during surgery at the age of 49. Mao Zongdong wrote the famous essay 'In Memory of Norman Bethune,' highly praising his internationalist spirit, making him a well-known international friend in China.

supporter.zh: 白求恩被视为伟大的国际主义者和人道主义典范。他放弃优渥的生活，两次奔赴战场，为西班牙和中国革命提供医疗援助。他的无私奉献精神、精湛医术和对医疗公平的追求，激励了无数人。白求恩不仅是一位医疗先驱，更是将医学与社会责任完美结合的典范，他的精神跨越国界，成为全人类共同的精神财富。
supporter.en: Bethune is regarded as a great internationalist and humanitarian model. He abandoned a comfortable life to go to battlefields twice, providing medical aid to the Spanish and Chinese revolutions. His selfless dedication, superb medical skills, and pursuit of medical fairness have inspired countless people. Bethune was not only a medical pioneer but also a perfect example of combining medicine with social responsibility. His spirit transcends borders, becoming a common spiritual treasure for all humanity.

critic.zh: 批评者认为白求恩的政治立场过于激进，将医疗工作与政治意识形态紧密相连。有人质疑他前往西班牙和中国战场的动机，认为他更关注政治宣传而非纯粹的医疗人道主义。此外，他的医疗创新虽然重要，但在现代医学史上的实际影响有限。批评者也指出，白求恩对中国医疗系统的了解有限，他的工作更多是象征性的而非系统性的改革。
critic.en: Critics argue that Bethune's political stance was too radical, closely linking medical work with political ideology. Some question his motives for going to the battlefields in Spain and China, suggesting he focused more on political propaganda than purely humanitarian medical work. Additionally, while his medical innovations were important, their actual impact on modern medical history is limited. Critics also point out that Bethune's understanding of China's healthcare system was limited, and his work was more symbolic than systematic reform.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，白求恩被定义为跨越国界的人道主义象征。他的故事被简化为国际主义精神的代表，毛泽东的《纪念白求恩》使他成为中国教育体系中的道德楷模。历史学家则更全面地看待他，既肯定他对战地医疗的贡献，也分析其政治背景和时代局限性。白求恩的形象在加拿大和中国有着不同的解读，反映了不同国家对历史记忆的选择性构建。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Bethune is defined as a symbol of humanitarianism that transcends borders. His story has been simplified as a representation of internationalist spirit, and Mao's 'In Memory of Norman Bethune' has made him a moral model in China's education system. Historians take a more comprehensive view, acknowledging his contributions to battlefield medicine while analyzing his political background and historical limitations. Bethune's image has different interpretations in Canada and China, reflecting selective historical memory construction by different nations.

self.zh: 我唯一的希望是能够多做贡献，能够帮助那些需要帮助的人。
self.en: My only hope is to be able to do more, to help those who need help.

others.zh: 一个高尚的人，一个纯粹的人，一个有道德的人，一个脱离了低级趣味的人，一个有益于人民的人。
others.en: A man of noble character, a pure man, a man of moral integrity, a man who has freed himself from vulgar interests, a man who is beneficial to the people.
